title: Device code: enter the code
summary: The script-free key.plrs.im/device page a person opens on their phone or computer to sign in a TV, console or other device: code first in big mono groups, the anti-phishing line, Continue. It names no product before the code resolves; the next step (identity.device-confirm) always asks 'Sign in on <device>?'.
compare: Code first: the field is the first control, big mono groups with a dash that never wrap; paste of the whole code works, case and spaces don't matter (PX-14).
No product, art or developer before the code resolves (B9, portal report): the card has no app header; Polaris Key's brand line only.
The anti-phishing line sits between the code and Continue: 'Only use a code from your own product, not one somebody sent you.' (B12)
Script-free Worker page: a form POST with an origin check, escaped echo of the code, no countdown (the device shows 'Expires at …'); no inline style or script (auth-14).
Errors (identity.device-code-states): a wrong code says so at the field; an expired one says the device shows a new code. Neither is a dead end.
The next step is always the explicit confirm (identity.device-confirm): a scan or a code is never approval (B9).
